lots.guide_summary: A composite lot, so the guide is the sum of each main title's range of surviving same or close entries: Bean vols I to VI A$188 to 900 (low: Davidson 2020 SOLD A$375 for 12 vols pro rata; high: Treloar ASK A$1,800 for 12 vols pro rata; Grant's asks A$418 for these six volumes), Little Black Princess A$79 to 1,200 (third printing ASK to Kay Craddock's 1905 first ASK; a 1905 first SOLD for A$280 at Leski in 2022), Modern Crusaders A$300 to 450 (ex-library ASK to a signed copy SOLD in Oct 2024), Tasmanian Literary Landmarks A$16.50 to 20 (ASK), A Book of Beauty no evidence; total A$583 to 2,570. Mix: 7 SOLD, all 2016 to Oct 2024 at Melbourne and Sydney rooms; 0 UNSOLD; the rest dealer ASKING. Tasmania: Gowans has none of these titles; its WWI and official history sets made A$40 to 110. Leski and all 78 Davidson sales were checked for these titles. Armitage's own results could not be searched (WebSearch cap). Rates: open.er-api.com, updated 19 Oct 2026 00:02 UTC: GBP 1 = A$1.91397, USD 1 = A$1.43581, EUR 1 = A$1.61297, A$1 = 109.949 JPY. AbeBooks listings from Australian sellers are given in the seller's own A$ price (AbeBooks converts at 0.71544 USD per AUD).
lots.working: No SOLD evidence in the last 24 months for any part of the lot: Leski Bean results 30 May 2021 and 4 Dec 2022, Mossgreen Bean set 28 Nov 2016, Davidson Bean set 24 May 2020, Leski Gunn 1905 first 28 Mar 2022, Leski Gunn 1906 mixed lot 28 May 2023, and Davidson Modern Crusaders 14 Oct 2024, which falls 24 months and 5 days before today and was a signed association copy. So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. For scale only (old results): Bean vols I to VI about A$190 to 360 at A$31 to 60 a volume, Gunn 1905 first A$280 hammer, Modern Crusaders A$450 hammer for a signed copy; Hobart sold comparable WWI history sets for A$40 to 110. Armitage premium 22% including GST; inbound freight $0 (pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).
lots.confidence_reason: Titles read in the photos, but the Gunn's imprint (first printing or not) and the Bean printings are unseen, and no SOLD evidence falls within 24 months; values rest on old mainland results and dealer asks.
lots.dropped_entries: Gowans record 423328, Manning Clark A History of Australia 6 vols (SOLD A$50): verified (5000 cents, 0 bids, listed 12 Jul 2026) and photo checked, but a modern, common set unrelated to WWI or these titles: dropped as not informative. Kept with corrections: Leski sale 467 lot 914 sold Sunday 30 May 2021, not 4 Jun 2021; Leski sale 486 lot 707 sold Sunday 4 Dec 2022, not 9 Dec; Leski sale 491 lot 976 sold Sunday 28 May 2023, not 27 May (session times on the sale info pages). Lazarus Books copy is in blue cloth, so moved from close to category guide; the Leski 6-book lot moved from close to category guide because the Gunn's share is unknown. Photo note corrected: the brighter red Bean volume appears to be vol VI, not vol IV. The researcher's Larsen Books US$8 Tasmanian Literary Landmarks copy had no URL and is not used. Gowans '3 Australian in the War sets' (A$45) checked and found to be penny coin sets, not books.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: six Bean volumes in maroon cloth with gilt spines reading VOL I and VOL II The Story of Anzac and VOL III The A.I.F. in France 1916, then (left to right) VOL VI and VOL V The A.I.F. in France 1918 and VOL IV 1917, Angus & Robertson at the feet. The fourth, brighter red volume appears to read VOL VI (the 1942 only edition) rather than vol IV; the labels are small, so check at viewing. Modern Crusaders in orange/tan cloth lettered With the Light Horse through Sinai and Palestine. The Little Black Princess in light green pictorial cloth lettered BY JEANNIE GUNN, matching the Kay Craddock 1905 first edition photos (spine foot THE DE LA MORE PRESS), whereas the September 1906 third printing (Renaissance Books photo) reads BY Mrs AENEAS GUNN. The lot's title page has the same setting as the 1905 first, but its imprint, the spine foot and the last leaf are not shown. A Book of Beauty in a chipped red patterned jacket, label subtitle illegible. Tasmanian Literary Landmarks title page inscribed 'To Mollie - best wishes, Margaret Giordano'.
lots.condition: Bean volumes: cloth bright with clear gilt, top edges dusty, interiors unseen. Modern Crusaders: cloth soiled and darkened, corners worn. Little Black Princess: cloth rubbed and soiled at the edges, spine and hinges unseen. A Book of Beauty: jacket chipped and torn at the edges. Tasmanian Literary Landmarks: clean paperback.
lots.question_for_armitage: For The Little Black Princess, please check the imprint at the foot of the title page (1905 or 1906) and its back, the spine foot (De La More Press or Melville and Mullen), whether the text ends with a colophon on p.108 (first printing) or with press opinions (later printing), and that the 24 plates and map are present and the hinges sound. For the Bean volumes, the edition dates on the title-page backs and any ex-library marks or foxing; for Modern Crusaders, the date on the title page and whether the folding map is present; and the compiler and publisher of A Book of Beauty.

lots.what_it_is: Pictorial painted bark cloth (tapa, called siapo or ngatu) from Wallis (Uvea), Wallis and Futuna, about 53 x 200 cm, in two scenes: a village scene (house, seated women with shell necklaces, a standing woman, pineapple, palms, flowers) and a sea scene (outrigger sailing canoe with 'Mua Wallis' on the sail, lobster, crab, octopus, fish, ray), with wavy red-brown and black and white geometric borders and black cloth hanging sleeves at both ends. Mua is a district of Wallis, so the title's 'by Mua Wallis' misreads a place name as a maker.
lots.score_reason: Credible identification as a rare pictorial Wallis type (Te Papa holds a near twin attributed to the 1960s), but the realistic Australian auction value is modest: generic tapa made A$10 to A$320 in the last 24 months, an early pictorial Tongan cloth passed at A$500, and a near-identical Wallis land-sea runner passed at EUR 80 in 2010. The upside is in a specialist Pacific sale (Webb's sold a smaller pictorial Uvea piece for NZD 950 in 2023). Scored for roughly A$150 to A$400, discounted for unverified age and the optimistic dealer ask.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop of photo 3 reads 'Mua Wallis' on the canoe sail (a place inscription, not a signature). The composition matches Te Papa FE012568 (record opened, https://collections.tepapa.govt.nz/object/1086286: Wallis and Futuna, attributed to the 1960s, 762 x 1985 mm, 'a rare example of tapa decorated with pictorial references', the same canoe with 'Mua Wallis' on the sail and a village scene, bought from a French brocante in 2010, no price) and the 1stdibs dealer piece (same two-scene layout, island name on the canoe). It also resembles a narrow 'terre-mer' Wallis runner (43 x 165 cm) that passed at EUR 80 in Marseille in 2010, which suggests a repeated decorative or trade type rather than a one-off. Black sleeves are stitched to both ends for hanging; the dark red-brown pigment is glossy (a traditional glossy dye or a later coating, not determinable from the photos).
lots.condition: Looks intact in the photos, with no holes or tears visible; creases, folds and wavy uneven edges; glossy finish on the dark pigment; hanging sleeves stitched on. The back is not shown, so staining, insect damage, brittleness or repairs cannot be judged. Age unverified.

Stone looks like a fine pale limestone or very pale sandstone. Age and origin unproven: Gothic or Gothic Revival European, or a later garden or architectural copy are all possible.
lots.condition: Heavily weathered and pitted, leaf tips and ring edges worn or chipped, a hairline crack or seam on the front, orange iron staining on the back. Back is flat cut. No size given; it looks roughly 20 cm across.
lots.key_photo_findings: Five originals re-checked. Photos 2 and 3 show the flat sawn back with a round drilled hole (fixing or lifting hole). Photo 5 shows the moulded ringed stem and foliate bowl clearly. No mark, mason's mark or date seen. Background in photos 1 and 2 shows Chinese scroll paintings, so the consignment may include Asian pieces; a Chinese or garden origin cannot be ruled out. The ticket string hides part of the stem.

Australian auction results in the last 24 months are A$300 to A$1,250 hammer (median about A$440), so a real value of roughly A$300 to A$600 at a local auction. Serial number not visible. Photo 1: tall black case with the foot controller clipped in the lid, a tan box (looks empty), a box of presser feet and attachments, a white box holding two metal embroidery hoop rings, and a red tray. lots.what_it_is: Box of Sydney and aviation ephemera. It includes an 'In Memoriam' order of service for Flight-Lieut. Keith Anderson, Royal Air Force (killed in the Kookaburra while searching for Kingsford Smith), Mosman Presbyterian Church, 6th July 1929 (read in photo 2); old Sydney Morning Herald, Daily Telegraph and Evening News newspapers; a clipping headed 'Maps and ... How News Will Come, tracing the flight of a giant bird' (likely 1928 Southern Cross coverage); a Sydney Harbour Bridge colour print and a crowd photo print; a bound illustrated Boer War periodical volume (caption 'Major Robin and Adjutant, New Zealand Contingent', credited to the Sphere); and a LIFE International special double issue 'The World in Our Time, a Pictorial Atlas for the Space Age'.

SOLD: Hobart A$65 to A$90 for one stepped opal shade or one complete stepped pendant; Leonard Joel A$250 for a two-shade chrome opal pendant; Nordic 1930s chrome three or four light opal fittings A$290 to A$537 each, with an outlier at A$887. lots.working: No exact twin sold, so the lowest lot-scale close SOLD is used as a conservative floor: Leonard Joel IT122 lot 185, A$250 hammer (24 Mar 2026), one two-shade chrome opal Deco pendant. Lot 239 holds two fittings and about seven stepped shades, more than that lot, but needs assembly and rewiring, so A$250 for the pair is a fair floor. keep_max = 250 / 1.22 = 204.9, round down to $200 hammer ($244 all-in). Flip: likely resale about A$300 hammer for the pair sold unwired in an Australian room (above the single Leonard Joel pendant, well under Nordic per-fitting prices of A$290 to A$537 because ours is unwired and in parts), less about 15% auction commission = A$255; 255 / 2.44 = 104.5, round down to $100 hammer. Inbound freight $0 (local pickup at Invermay). Rewiring by a licensed electrician is extra and not costed here; it would cut the flip margin.
lots.confidence_reason: No maker mark read, view partial (fittings unassembled, shade count and arm count uncertain), age unclear (very bright chrome could mean replating or a later copy), and no same-item SOLD: max bids rest on close-class sales, mostly Nordic.

lots.what_it_is: Large three-section illuminated ceramic Christmas tree in the Atlantic Mold style: glossy green glaze with dark streaking, tiered top, wide skirt tier, and a white base moulded and hand painted as wrapped presents with a toy train. Coloured plastic peg bulbs including red and blue bird shapes; cord attached. No mould mark visible (underside not shown), so possibly an unmarked hobby-ceramic tree rather than genuine Atlantic Mold.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 (whole tree) and photo 2 (close-up of branches) re-checked. Three parts visible: top tree, skirt tier, white presents-and-train base; cord exits the base at right. Bird bulbs in red and blue plus round and flame pegs in red, orange, yellow, green and blue. No chips, cracks or missing pegs seen on the visible faces; no star topper visible. No mark, signature or date can be read anywhere; base underside not photographed. Base painting looks hand done, typical of 1970s-80s hobby ceramics classes. Size not stated.
lots.condition: Looks clean and complete on the visible faces; no obvious chips or repairs. Electrics untested. Back of tree, underside and mark not shown; check every peg is present and the sections sit together without cracks.
lots.score_reason: A popular nostalgic collectable type; verified US auction results for large lit ceramic trees cluster about US$50 to US$110 (A$72 to A$158), with outliers to US$200. Unusual presents-and-train base may help, but no mark is visible and there is no Australian sales record, so mid band.

lots.guide_summary: Same item or close: 14 sold, 0 unsold, 4 asking. Same item inside 24 months, all US auctions: US$60, US$85 and US$125 (A$86 to A$180). Same item outside the window: A$20 at Lawsons Sydney (03/10/2024, the only Australian sale found, generic title), US$90 twice and US$35 with wear (2024, US). Close (Butterfly Gold trios, or sets with round bowls or extra pieces): US$50 to US$150 (A$72 to A$216). Asking: four live US Poshmark listings, US$199 to US$350 (A$286 to A$503), not prices paid. Category only: Australian rooms paid A$35 to A$140 for other retro Pyrex (A$25 and A$120 passed in), and Gowans mixed lots with one Butterfly Gold casserole made $55 and $80. USD at 1.437 (ECB, 16/10/2026).
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD inside 24 months in similar condition = US$60 (Matthew Bullock lot 12, 22/11/2025) x 1.437 = A$86.22; / 1.22 = $70.67, round down to $70 hammer ($85.40 all-in). Flip: likely resale about A$86 (that same lowest in-window sale; the higher US results are out of reach from Tasmania because posting four glass bowls overseas costs too much), less about 15% selling fees ($12.93) and $0 postage (local pickup sale) = $73.29; / 2.44 = $30.04, round down to $30. Caution: every in-window sale is American. The only Australian sale of this exact set made A$20 (Lawsons, 03/10/2024, 16 days outside the window) and Australian rooms paid A$35 to A$70 for other retro Pyrex nests and trios, so treat $70 as a ceiling and expect it may sell well below. Pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay; inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Pattern and set make-up are read clearly in the photos and there are three same-item SOLD results inside 24 months (pages opened; prices from Invaluable's own index because the pages hide them behind a login), but all are US sales, the only Australian same-item sale was A$20, and the bases (marks, chips, wear) are not photographed.

lots.what_it_is: Seven timber cupboard doors and panels (four routed cathedral-arch doors with porcelain knobs and brass hinges, three loose panels), titled as Huon pine. Species not confirmed: at least one door has dark knots with reddish rings typical of radiata or Baltic pine. The routed arch style is typical of 1980s-90s kitchen joinery.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo re-checked; crop of the third door from left enlarged: it shows two dark knots and broad, wavy grain consistent with radiata pine rather than the fine, knot-light grain usual in Huon pine. lots.guide_summary: Close entries run $15 to $500 (all AUD, every page opened). SOLD: 11 close results, Feb 2025 to Sep 2026, $50 to $500 hammer or Invaluable sold amount, median about $110 with the E J Ainger table counted once; plain mahogany tables made $50 to $300, walnut-topped ones $80 to $500. The only Tasmanian close sale is Gowans $50 after three passes. UNSOLD: 8 close tables passed in at last bids of $15 to $260 (one Gowans pass shows no amount), and several only sold after repeated passes and estimate cuts. ASKING: none kept. Category guides (burr or inlaid walnut tops, three-legged or round tripod tables) sold $150 to $650 and do not set the range. Invaluable figures may or may not include premium. No currency conversion needed.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD in the last 24 months in similar condition is $50 (Vickers & Hoad 8 Mar 2026, and Gowans 26 Jun 2026). 50 / 1.22 = 40.98, round down to $40 hammer ($48.80 all-in with Armitage's 22% premium incl GST). Flip: likely resale about $110 hammer (median of the close SOLD set: 50, 50, 80, 95, 100, 120, 170, 300, 300, 500, counting the E J Ainger table once), less about 15% vendor commission (assumed, not verified, $16.50) and $0 postage (local auction resale, buyer collects) = $93.50; 93.50 / 2.44 = 38.3, round down to $35. Flip margin is thin: tables of this kind passed in repeatedly at Gowans, Woodlands, Leonard Joel, Lawsons and Aalders. Pickup only from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay; inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Form and period are clear and 11 close SOLD records were opened (10 Invaluable pages plus a Gowans record with photos), but furniture of this kind carries no mark to read, the top timber and tilt action are unconfirmed, and the refinished top, edge split and mismatched frieze need a look in person.
lots.score_reason: A real mid-Victorian carved loo table, but close Australian sales mostly run $50 to $300 (median about $110) and lot 390 has a refinished top, an edge split and a frieze that does not match. Worth about $80 to $200, so 5.
lots.key_photo_findings: Three photos checked with enlarged crops. One-piece oval top with a moulded edge in a straight-grained reddish timber, refinished with a patchy orange-brown polish, small dark spots, and a short break or join in the edge moulding at the front (photo 3). The frieze is a much paler honey-coloured figured timber with a visible vertical joint, unlike the top and base, so it may be a different or replacement timber, or the top has been stained darker. Ring-turned and gadrooned baluster column with a dark collar; four leaf-carved, scroll-shouldered cabriole legs ending in scroll toes; white ceramic castors on all four legs. No underside, tilt catch, label or stamp shown. At 117 x 87 cm it is smaller than most comparables (134 to 154 cm long).
lots.condition: Base looks sound and complete, carving crisp, all four castors present. Top refinished, patchy and faded, with small dark marks and a split or join in the front edge moulding. Frieze timber does not match the top or base. Tilt mechanism, column joint and underside not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does the top tilt and does the catch work, and is the column firm with no wobble or repaired legs? What timber is the top, solid or veneered, and is the pale frieze original or a replacement (if the table is Australian cedar, blackwood or Huon pine rather than English mahogany it would interest local buyers more)? Is the mark at the front edge a crack or an old join? Are all four ceramic castors original and turning?

lots.what_it_is: Mixed box of unmarked decorative ware, 7 pieces: (1) South-East Asian style long-stem smoking ('opium') pipe, about 40 cm, elephant-head bowl with trunk, tusks, ear rings, bell on a chain, filigree cage knop and wire bands, yellowish white metal or brass alloy, no mark visible; (2) pair of pale celadon crackle-glaze twin-handled vases (modern decorator); (3) single one-light gilt metal tole-style candle branch with two painted ceramic or resin parrots and flowers on a black and gilt base; (4) pair of Murano-style glass lovebirds on a clear base; (5) large ribbed oval clear glass bowl with frosted leaf handles holding about 12 faceted crystal balls; (6) heavy octagonal clear crystal dish or ashtray; (7) small green majolica-style leaf dish.
lots.score_reason: Decorative box whose value rests on the pipe and the parrot candle branch. The pipe form (wirework knop, animal bowl) sells about A$45 to 110 at European online rooms as white metal; the parrot branch is a single one-light piece of a design that sells in pairs for A$290 to 380 in the UK, so a single is likely well under half that. The rest is A$10 to 50 Gowans-level decorator glass and celadon. A realistic combined auction value is roughly A$100 to 200, more only if the pipe proves to be silver.

lots.guide_summary: Mostly SOLD. Close whole-lot comparables (tubs or boxes of built modern LEGO) sold for $55 to $130 hammer in Tasmania between Feb and Oct 2026: Armitage $80 and $105 (8 Jul 2026), Gowans $55 to $130 (7 lots). Same-item component sales (US eBay via PriceCharting, built or loose, no box): Dobby A$7.19 to A$28.74 (typical A$14), Mandrake A$24.66 to A$50.28 (typical A$29), Aragog A$4.67 to A$10.42, and the three orphan Speed Champions booklets A$10.06 to A$14.37 each; the identified parts add up to about A$75 at the lowest and A$91 at typical prices, before fees and postage. Category guides (other Armitage and Gowans LEGO lots, two boxed sets, bulk tubs, train lots) ran $35 to $150 hammer. No UNSOLD result found. ASKING: only the Brickset model values (used about US$15 to 28 a set). The guide range ($55 to $130) is the close whole-lot evidence. Hammer prices exclude buyer's premium (Armitage 22%; Gowans premium extra). USD at 1.437 (ECB via frankfurter.dev, 16 Oct 2026).
lots.working: Keep, from same-item SOLD sales (built or loose, no box, last 24 months), lowest of each item, US$ at 1.437: Dobby 76421 US$5.00 = A$7.19, Mandrake 76433 US$17.16 = A$24.66 (the US$9.99 glued sale is dropped as not comparable), Aragog 76434 US$3.25 = A$4.67, booklets 76914 US$10.00 = A$14.37, 76921 US$7.00 = A$10.06 and 76907 US$9.99 = A$14.36. Total A$75.31 / 1.22 = $61.73, round down = $60. Cross-check: Tasmanian close tubs of built LEGO made $55 to $130 hammer (Armitage $80 and $105), so $60 sits at the low end of what these rooms pay; the train panels, flowers, Friends builds and loose bricks are not valued. Flip, parting out on eBay AU at typical sold prices: Dobby A$14.37 (US$10) + Mandrake A$28.74 (US$20) + Aragog A$8.62 (US$6) + booklets A$14.37 + A$10.06 + A$14.36 = A$90.52, less eBay fees of about 13% (A$11.77) and outbound postage of about A$49 (three parcels at A$10 to 15, three large letters at about A$4) = A$29.75 / 2.44 = $12.19, round down = $10. Buyer's premium 22% incl. GST (all-in = hammer x 1.22); pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Dobby and Mandrake match Brickset images closely and the booklet numbers 76921 and 76914 are read, with many matching SOLD results opened (PriceCharting sold lists and Tasmanian hammer prices on past catalogue pages and the Gowans API). Held at Medium because completeness and condition are unknown, Aragog is very likely but not certain, the component sales are US eBay prices, and much of the tub is unidentified.

lots.question_for_armitage: Are there any minifigures in the tub (especially Harry and Ron from the Aragog set)? Are Dobby's diary accessory and the Mandrake's name tile there, and are the Dobby, Mandrake or Aragog instruction booklets included (the text booklet marked WI)? Roughly how full and heavy is the tub, and are there any non-LEGO bricks mixed in?

lots.what_it_is: Avon 1876 Cape Cod ruby red pressed glass (Avon's collectable range sold from 1975 to the mid 1990s), identified by the pattern (diamond-hatched heart band, starburst centres, scalloped rims, hexagonal feet) and the catalogue title (2 BOXES OF AVON GLASS - DINNER WARE, NAPKIN RINGS, ETC). About 60 to 80 pieces: a tall stack of dinner plates, further stacks of smaller plates, two stacks of rimmed soup or dessert bowls, a larger bowl, the big diamond-cut serving bowl, 4 footed (pedestal) mugs, 5 hexagonal-base salt or pepper shakers, about 13 napkin rings, a dinner plate displayed upright and a small hexagonal tray with gold script and a gold flower motif (unread). No AVON base marks are visible (bases not shown; some Cape Cod pieces are marked). Lot 470 in the same sale is a further 3 boxes of the same pattern (per the prep notes).
lots.score_reason: A large collection of a recognised collectable Avon pattern; US asks of about US$5 to 12 a piece suggest a real value above $80 for 60 to 80 pieces, but there is no sold price, Tasmanian ruby glass sells for $30 to $50 or passes in, and more of the same pattern (lot 470) is in this sale: 5.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item SOLD or UNSOLD result exists. The guide range (A$212.68 to A$359.25) is three Poshmark US asking prices for 20 to 26 piece Avon Cape Cod sets (one live and unsold after five weeks, two marked sold at the list price, one of those from 2024), each about a third the size of lot 468; component asks run about US$4 to US$17.50 a piece. Tasmanian evidence is much weaker: 6 SOLD category guides at $20 to $50 hammer (plain ruby or red glass lots, plus one small mixed Avon lot with two Cape Cod candlesticks at $20) and 3 UNSOLD passes of plain ruby goblets at Gowans in May 2026. Of the 21 surviving entries, 6 are sold (all category guides), 3 unsold and 12 asking. USD at 1.437 (ECB via frankfurter.dev, 16 Oct 2026).

lots.guide_summary: All AUD hammer, no conversion (rate 1.00). 8 close SOLD: Armitage's own room $25, $80 and $125 (Jul to Sep 2026) and Gowans $35 to $130 (Feb to Aug 2026). The three with about the same Carlton content as lot 563 (5 to 7 floral leaf pieces) made $35 (Gowans 416349), $50 (Gowans 408739) and $80 (Armitage lot 452, which also had uranium glass and decanters); larger all-Carlton groups made $90 to $130. Category guides, all SOLD: mixed china with a Carlton share $3 to $90; generic two-box china lots $25 to $100. Four Gowans lots naming Carlton passed in (420091 and its re-offer 421718, 422742 and its re-offer 424364) with no bid amount shown, so they are noted but not listed. No ASKING evidence found.
lots.working: Same-item set = lots with about the same Carlton content as lot 563 (5 to 7 floral leaf pieces) sold in the last 24 months: $35 (Gowans 416349, 19 Jun 2026), $50 (Gowans 408739, 15 May 2026) and $80 (Armitage lot 452, 9 Sep 2026). Keep: lowest $35 / 1.22 = $28.69, rounded down to $25 hammer ($30.50 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $50 hammer (median of the three), less an assumed 15% vendor commission ($7.50) and $0 outbound postage (resold through a local auction, buyer collects) = $42.50; / 2.44 = $17.42, rounded down to $15. Inbound freight $0 (pickup at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay). The filler porcelain adds little. A flip has almost no margin, so this is a small keep buy only.
lots.confidence_reason: The moulded pattern clearly matches Carlton Ware Australian Design Apple Blossom-type ware (the same pieces appear in Armitage lot 452 and in Gowans lots with backstamps), and three same-content SOLD results were opened, one in Armitage's own room. Not High because no backstamp is visible in the single photo and condition cannot be checked.

Enlarged: Carlton Ware Australian Design moulded leaf ware with brown twig handles and pink star blossoms with yellow centres (Apple Blossom type, pattern name not confirmed): large green triangular leaf dish, green oval leaf bowl, small green leaf dish, green cream jug, and a yellow triangular leaf tray holding an egg-shaped salt and pepper pair. The rest is mixed gilt-edged porcelain: about a dozen small jugs, a cake plate with roses, a scenic plate on a stand, a Japanese-style cup and saucer, a small character jug, a vase and a pot. lots.what_it_is: Seven-drawer twin-pedestal kneehole desk (three drawers across the top including a long centre frieze drawer, two more under each end) in figured reddish-brown mahogany-type veneer, with pyramid timber knobs, a low back gallery, plinth bases and a loose glass top, plus a plain splat-back chair with a cream seat. 1930s to 1940s style. The pale drawer linings fit the catalogue's 'Huon pine secondaries' but cannot be confirmed from a photo, and no 'Hewett & Inglis' label or stamp shows in any photo (the researcher could not trace the firm).
lots.score_reason: A sound pedestal desk of this size with a chair is likely worth about $80 to $150 hammer in Tasmania (tidy pedestal desks at Gowans made $110 to $150), but plain ones have gone for $10 to $45, and the maker and Huon pine claims are unconfirmed.

Category guides, not in the range: SOLD $360 (solid Huon pine desk) and $475 (19th century cedar and Huon pine 7 drawer desk); ASKING US$1,456 (about A$2,092 at 1.437) from a US dealer. Armitage's own past results could not be searched because the shared WebSearch cap was already used up.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD: none of the Gowans desks is a 1930s to 1940s veneered seven-drawer desk with Huon pine linings. They are later reproductions, other timbers or worn office desks, and they range from $10 to $220, so they are guides only and no maximum is set (keep 0, flip 0). As a guide only, a tidy pedestal desk of this size makes about $110 to $150 hammer in Tasmania ($134.20 to $183 all-in at Armitage's 22%), and a plain one can go for $10 to $45. If the viewing confirms Huon pine linings, a maker's label and a sound chair, it would sit at the top of that guide. Inbound freight $0 (pickup from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay).
lots.confidence_reason: No maker's mark or label read in the photos, the Huon pine is unconfirmed, and there is no same-item SOLD result, only category results of different eras, styles and timbers.

(2) UNSOLD Gowans 375645 (19th century cedar and Huon pine 7 drawer desk, 21/11/2025): the same colonial desk as the kept $475 entry, passed in before it was relisted; it says nothing about lot 579, so it is mentioned in the $475 note instead. Corrected: 436930 has a tooled leather inset top, not a plain top. Added: Gowans 379756 ($20, older worn 8 drawer twin-pedestal desk). All Gowans dates are now exact sale dates from the auction records, not 'about a week after listing'. Every kept entry's record was opened and its title, price and bid count match the researcher's claims.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: seven drawers with pyramid-shaped timber knobs, figured reddish-brown striped veneer, arched kneehole, low back gallery, plinth bases and a loose glass top. Photo 1: small brass key in a drawer lock; plain splat-back chair in a similar reddish timber with a cream upholstered seat; the cabriole-leg chest behind is not part of the lot. Photo 2, enlarged: drawer lined in pale, fine-grained, honey-coloured timber consistent with Huon pine but not confirmable from a photo, with a brass lock-keeper strip. No maker's label, stamp or 'Hewett & Inglis' mark visible anywhere.
lots.condition: Veneer looks sound with ordinary age wear and no obvious loss or lifting; polish a little dull; glass top loose but apparently intact; drawer interior clean; chair seat clean. Back, underside, runners and chair joints not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a Hewett & Inglis label, stamp or any maker's mark on the desk or chair? What is the main timber, and are the drawer linings Huon pine? What are the overall dimensions? Is the glass top included and uncracked, do all seven drawers run freely, and is there a working key? Is the chair sound?
